description: GRAPH-RESIDENT: the CONFIDENT-WRONG-OUTSIDE-ITS-RANGE guard, authored by the jabberwock via the composer (CLAUDE.md discipline: no hand-written agent rule). Theory: a cheap-model basin-snap that is confidently WRONG has LOW residual within its own basin, so residual alone cannot catch it; what DOES distinguish it from a genuinely-solved collapse is whether its grounding chain reaches something EXTERNAL to the agent's own generative loop (an anchor) or loops back into itself. domains/grounding_reach.py's flag_ungrounded_confident already computes exactly that discriminator (low residual + high confidence + grounding_reach(node).reached is False) and mints a GroundingGap node -- mechanical adapter I/O, not a decision. THIS seed is the agent's OWN response to that flag: mints ONE rule, escalate_grounding_gap_<tag>, from an agent -wants_grounding_guard_rule-> ComposeRequest trigger (ground_concern's 'escalate' relation head, seeds/relation_vocabulary.json's new grounding_escalate cue + seeds/composer_dispatch.json's new ComposerCue). The minted rule matches every agent -has_grounding_gap-> gap edge (the mechanical exposure of an already-flagged GroundingGap to the rule engine -- domains/reflective_faculty.py's ensure_grounding_gap_edges, the SAME idempotent trigger-wiring idiom induce_concern uses for agent -observed-> observation) not yet escalated (gap.escalated is null), and -- instead of trusting the cheap snap -- mints an Impasse{kind:'grounding_gap'} and wires agent -surprised_by-> impasse (+ impasse -about_gap-> gap), REUSING the standing surprised_by/Impasse escalation channel this codebase already uses everywhere active cognition is engaged (seeds/impasse_escalation.json, seeds/investigation_teacher.json, seeds/self_extension.json): when seeds/autonomy.json's mint_goal_from_surprise is also loaded, that ALREADY-SEEDED rule turns the surprised_by edge into a wanted Goal on its own -- this seed does not reimplement 'unexplained -> goal', it plugs a GroundingGap into that existing channel. A node that flag_ungrounded_confident never flags (because its grounding chain DOES reach an anchor) never gets a has_grounding_gap edge, so this rule never touches it -- trust is the default; escalation is what a genuine gap earns. Marks gap.escalated so a re-run never re-escalates the same gap (fixpoint safety, the same guard idiom composer_control_graph's default_no_response uses).

effect.why: confident and low-residual, but the grounding chain does not reach an external anchor -- escalate to active cognition, do not trust the snap
